messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Help with independent records
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I believe the problem is that the date/time format in DateTimeOriginal does not match the expectation, since the date is sorted as DMY (instead of YMD) and the time is missing the seconds. I suppose you may have saved it in Excel in the meantime? Excel always removes the seconds. It may also have changed the date format.

Since assessTemporalIndependence is an internal function it doesn't check the date/time format. So what you'd need to do is reformat DateTimeOriginal to the expected format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS

Do this by combining the Photo.Date and Photo.Time columns, and take care to change Date to YMD instead of DMY.

To be sure I'd need to know the error message you received though.
Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Finding tags in specific folder
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
when you say "I can't see those tags in the folder where I am storing the camera trap photos", do you mean in Windows Explorer? That is normal. I think Explorer only shows XMP:Keywords, but the digiKam tags are written in the HierarchicalSubject metadata slot. That may be a little inconvenient, but should be no problem.
What is more important is that the tags are saved in the metadata of the image. You can check that with exifTagNames(). Search for the "HierarchicalSubject" tag group and see if the values contain the tags you assigned in digiKam.
If the tags are there, you can run recordTable() and other functions which read out the metadata tags assigned in digiKam

Regarding the second comment, there may be a misunderstanding regarding using metadata tags for species ID (which currently requires digiKam) vs. using species directories. When using species directories, you don't need digiKam (but there are also some drawbacks, see vignette 2). If you use metadata tags, you need digiKam (or possibly Adobe Bridge).
Exiftool and digiKam serve very different purposes. digiKam is most useful for tagging images with a nice user interface and lots of powerful image management options. Exiftool is a command line tool that can read image metadata and the tags assigned in digiKam, and R can then use the output of Exiftool for making record tables etc. So it's really two very different pieces of software, and Exiftool can't do the tagging for you.

If this doesn't answer your question please let us know or share some screenshots.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: imageRename function for videos
messages.body_plain:
Hi Robert,
imageRename currently only works for images, not videos. It should be possible, I just didn't get around to implement it yet. What you can consider doing is run recordTable with minDeltaTime = 0 (to get all images / videos), subset the table to contain only the videos, and use file.rename() to change the video filenames to whatever your heart desires (based on the columns in the record table). I imagine such a workaround should be feasible.
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Several Species tagged for one picture
messages.subject_clean: Several Species tagged for one picture
messages.body_plain:
Hi Isaure,
camtrapR only uses one species column, and if an image has several species it will results in several rows for the same image (recordTable does that automatically). So I think you'd need to convert your table to the standard format of camtrapR (see data("recordTableSample") and ?recordTable).
You can convert from your format (wide format) to  long  format used by camtrapR using e.g. reshape2::melt(). camtrapR does not offer a function for this task because the data structure you used is different from the camtrapR standard.

Also, What kind of "graph" do you need?

If you tagged the images with digiKam, you can probably create a new, properly formatted record table by running recordTable() instead of reformatting your existing table.

If this doesn't help please share a part of your table.

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: activityDensity
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sally,
see ?activityDensity. The last argument is ..., so any additional arguments are passed to overlap::densityPlot() - that's the underlying function doing the actual work. densityPlot has an argument "extend" which is 'lightgrey' by default. That's what you need to adjust.
So just add
extend = "white"
or
extend = NULL

to you activitDensity() call.
Best,
Jürgen
